sections.heading: 1. Force and Inertia
points: A **force** can change the **state of motion** or **shape** of an object.
**Balanced forces** = no change in motion; **unbalanced forces** = change motion.
**Inertia** = the tendency of an object to **resist a change** in its state of rest or motion; mass is a measure of inertia (more mass → more inertia).

sections.heading: 2. Newton's Laws of Motion
points: **First Law (Law of Inertia):** an object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by an **unbalanced force**.
**Second Law:** **Force = mass × acceleration (F = ma)**; force equals the rate of change of **momentum**. SI unit of force = **newton (N)**.
**Third Law:** to every action there is an **equal and opposite reaction** (forces act on **different** bodies).

sections.heading: 3. Momentum and its Conservation
points: **Law of conservation of momentum:** in the absence of external force, the **total momentum of a system stays constant**.
Examples: **recoil of a gun**, rocket propulsion, collisions.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Inertia = resistance to change in motion; mass = measure of inertia.
Newton's 1st law = law of inertia; needs an unbalanced force to change motion.
2nd law: F = ma (SI unit = newton); force = rate of change of momentum.
3rd law: action = reaction (equal & opposite, on different bodies).
Momentum = mass × velocity (kg·m/s); conserved when no external force acts.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Mass is the measure of inertia** — a heavier object has more inertia.
In Newton's **third law**, action and reaction act on **different** bodies, so they don't cancel.
**F = ma**; the SI unit of force is the **newton**.
**Momentum is conserved** only when **no external force** acts on the system.
